:::{#def-main-diagonal}
#### Main diagonal

The **main diagonal** of an $m \times n$ matrix $\matr{A}$
is the list of its entries $a_{11}, a_{22}, \ldots, a_{kk}$,
where $k$ is the smaller of $m$ and $n$.
These are the **diagonal entries** of $\matr{A}$;
every entry $a_{ij}$ with $i \ne j$ is an **off-diagonal entry**.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-main-diagonal}
#### Diagonal entries of a square and a non-square matrix

- For $\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$,
  the diagonal entries are $a_{11} = 1$ and $a_{22} = 4$,
  and the off-diagonal entries are $a_{12} = 2$ and $a_{21} = 3$.
- For $\matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 5 & 6 \end{bmatrix}$,
  $m = 2$ and $n = 3$, so $k = 2$,
  and the diagonal entries are $b_{11} = 1$ and $b_{22} = 5$;
  the other four entries, $2$, $3$, $4$ and $6$, are off-diagonal.

:::
